\section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}

The paper gives a closed-form record-law and fixed-setting asymptotic analysis
for one constrained latched killed-leakage sampled-counter D-MAP(2) subfamily.
The visible
record identifies the unordered survival/rate coordinates, not hidden labels
or response-side thermodynamic parameters without external calibration.  The
two-state fibre theorem makes this ambiguity exact in the larger killed-reset
class: separated rates generate a closed continuum arc whose only triangular
members are the two physical rate orderings, while equal rates generate a
singleton fibre.  The diagonal statement is deliberately narrow: it is only
the pointwise projected
limit at the fixed \(z_0=1/2\) candidate with its printed population covariance
certificate, and it carries no confidence-procedure interpretation.

The theorem-by-theorem comparison in
\Cref{sec:theorem-led-comparison} separates recalled proof inputs from the
model-specific calculations proved here.

\section{Related Work and Mathematical Comparison}\label{sec:theorem-led-comparison}

The introduction gives the mathematical narrative comparison with the closest
renewal-binary, weak-memory, waiting-time, partial-observation, and detector
papers.  This final section gives a compact theorem-by-theorem comparison with
the direct D-MAP, MAP, and discrete phase-type literature, followed by the
closest detector-model comparator.  Extended comparator tables and the search
ledger are placed in the supplementary material.

\subsection{Detector dead-time comparator}\label{subsec:detector-dead-time-comparator-main}

In the nonparalyzable continuous dead-time model, an accepted event is followed
by a fixed or random inactive period and then by a live waiting time; this
structure produces renewal count statistics and motivates classical
dead-time corrections and detector checks
\cite{YuFessler2000,SarbaziSafariHaas2018LongDeadTime,
GronbergDanielssonSjolin2018Nonparalyzable,MeeksSiegel2008DeadTime}.
Krause--Walenta's continuous exponential-recovery model for free-running SPADs
allows detection efficiency to recover continuously after dead time and fits
parameters from inter-detection intervals \cite{KrauseWalenta2025SPADRecovery}.
Such a detector need not have \(T_1(\cdot,R)=0\): after a click, physical
recovery and further evolution can occur before the next externally chosen bin
boundary.  In contrast, the present model is a sampled discrete D-MAP with
stochastic recovery before a click and an explicit post-click latch until the
boundary.
Its Palm zero-run law is
\[
g_k=e_D^\top T_0^kT_1\mathbf1
=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(1-p)p^k-\Gamma(1-s)s^k}
       {\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
\]
with the continuous equal-rate limit understood.  The contribution relative to
the detector dead-time literature is therefore not a generic dead-time
correction.  It is an exact quotient inverse for the sampled killed-leakage
D-MAP visible law, together with the renewal product and retained-record
covariance route that are valid only under the boundary-reset convention in
\Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main,prop:model-fragility-boundary-reset-main}.

\subsection{Theorem-by-theorem comparison with DMAP, DPH, and MAP theory}

\paragraph{Theorem A (record law).}
Alfa--Neuts supply the general D-MAP construction
\cite{AlfaNeuts1995DMAP}, while M\'esz\'aros--Telek study canonical
representations for general discrete order-two MAPs and RAPs
\cite{MeszarosTelek2013DiscreteMAP2Canonical}.  Those representation results
do not assert that the present triangular, deterministically reset subfamily is
renewal.  The additional calculation here is restricted to that subfamily: it
derives the Palm gap law, increasing hazard, one-mode covariance, and exact
\(1\)-dependence criterion.  These are elementary model-specific consequences,
not a new general DMAP theorem.

\paragraph{Theorem B (three-inclusion quotient inverse).}
The closest prior result is the canonical-coordinate analysis of discrete
order-two MAP/RAP models by M\'esz\'aros--Telek
\cite{MeszarosTelek2013DiscreteMAP2Canonical}, together with canonical MAP2
and matrix-exponential representation work
\cite{BodrogHeindlHorvathTelek2008MAP2Canonical,
TelekHorvath2007MinimalMAP}.  That literature constructs sparse or canonical
representatives and moment-matching maps for broader representation classes.
Theorem~B neither replaces nor strengthens those canonical-form theorems.  Its
narrow additional statement is the direct rational identity
\[
\frac{r_2-r_0^2}{r_1-r_0^2}=p-b
\]
for the latched killed-reset image, which converts three visible binary
inclusion probabilities into \((p+s,ps)\) and hence the complete visible
renewal law.  The estimand is a law-determining quotient, not a labelled
minimal DMAP2 representative.  We do not claim that this identity is absent as
an implicit specialization of canonical DMAP2 coordinates; the contribution
is the explicit three-inclusion specialization and its stability bounds.

\paragraph{Theorems C and D (asymptotics).}
The regenerative CLT, separated-batch method, and multivariate delta method are
standard inputs \cite{Zamparo2022RenewalBinary,Janson2024RenewalCLT,
AsmussenGlynn2007,FlegalJones2010BatchMeansSpectral}.  The paper's additional
work is bookkeeping for complete retained cycles, the explicit stopped-prefix
bounds, and transport to the three-inclusion quotient.  The sorted-root and
log-rate CLTs are direct delta-method consequences and are not claimed as new
asymptotic theory.

\paragraph{Theorem E (projection example).}
Metric-projection limits at smooth inequality boundaries are standard
\cite{Shapiro1987MetricProjection,FangSeo2021ProjectionTests}.  Theorem~E is
therefore presented only as a pointwise worked projection at \(z_0=1/2\), with
a reproducible covariance nondegeneracy certificate.  It makes no inferential
or novelty claim beyond this specialization.

\paragraph{Complete-law checking and the Markov--Palm score.}
Distributional-distance consistency, serial-independence basis tests,
finite-range and Hilbert-space central limit theorems, and local Gaussian
shift calculus are standard inputs
\cite{RyabkoRyabko2010ErgodicInference,Ryabko2012StationaryTesting,
SkaugTjostheim1993SerialIndependence,DedeckerMerlevede2003HilbertCLT,
vanDerVaart1998AsymptoticStatistics}.
\Cref{thm:complete-visible-law-specification-main} combines those inputs with
the sampled-counter word law and an explicit rank-one Markov-gap path.  The
model-specific extension in
\Cref{thm:complete-markov-palm-tangent-omnibus-main} is the exact closed
interaction space obtained by adding $q(0,0)=0$ to double centring, its
$\mu^{-1}$-scaled efficient projection, and the exchange-boundary calibration
of a trace-weighted score.  It claims pointwise strict local power in every
nonzero interaction direction, but neither a new general independence test
nor a uniform infinite-dimensional minimax envelope.

The growing-dimensional coupling invoked for the Helmert truncation is likewise
external: CMU's Corollaries~2.2--2.3 supply the
martingale and independent-vector Yurinskii bounds
\cite{CattaneoMasiniUnderwood2025Yurinskii}.  The model-specific calculation
checks their inputs.  Because those bounds retain an ambient-dimension factor,
\Cref{prop:helmert-growing-layer-bracket-main} states only the proved
necessary/sufficient bracket and leaves its logarithmic gap open.

\paragraph{Fibre results.}
Minimal-realization uniqueness is classical, beginning with Kalman and used
directly for MAP reduction and moment matching by Telek--Horv\'ath
\cite{Kalman1963LinearSystems,TelekHorvath2007MinimalMAP}.  Accordingly,
\Cref{thm:nstate-killed-reset-identifiability-dichotomy-main} is explicitly a
recalled orbit-fibre reformulation.  The new two-state assertion is
\Cref{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main}: for the physical triangular
kernel, the complete Markovian orbit intersection is an explicit closed arc
between the rate-swapped endpoints and collapses exactly on the exchange
diagonal.  General MAP2 nonidentifiability and weak-equivalence results are the
nearest representation-theoretic comparators
\cite{RamirezCoboLilloWiper2010MAP2Nonidentifiability,
RamirezCoboLillo2012WeakEquivalentMAP}; the claim here is only this exact
killed-reset sampled-counter specialization.

The further new assertion is
\Cref{thm:nstate-interior-continuum-nonidentifiability-main}: the unrestricted
interior fibre contains a positivity-preserving similarity manifold of exact
dimension \((n-1)^2\).  For serial kernels, Cumani's canonical failure-time
forms, acyclic DPH estimation, and order-two/three discrete PH canonical forms
are direct predecessors
\cite{Cumani1982CanonicalFailure,BobbioEtAl2003AcyclicDPH,
PappTelek2013DiscretePHCanonical,MeszarosPappTelek2014Traffic}.
\Cref{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main} is consequently
stated as a killed-reset orbit-intersection calculation: the pure serial fibre
is exactly the rate-multiset permutation class, with collisions handled by the
confluent recurrence.  It is not claimed as a new general acyclic-DPH
canonical-form theorem.  General phase-type nonuniqueness remains fully
consistent with O'Cinneide's invariant-polytope analysis
\cite{OCinneide1989PhaseTypeNonuniqueness,OCinneide1991InvariantPolytopes}.

 144: \begin{theorem}[Complete two-state fibre arc and exchange dichotomy]
 145: \label{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main}
 146: Under \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, put \(K=T_0\),
 147: \(q_\ast=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), and
 148: \[
 149:  I_\ast=[\min\{1,q_\ast\},\max\{1,q_\ast\}].
 150: \]
 151: Then \(K\) is minimal, and its complete visible-law fibre in
 152: \(\mathcal K_2\) is the injectively parametrized closed arc
 153: \[
 154:  \{K(q):q\in I_\ast\},
 155:  \qquad
 156:  K(q)=
 157:  \begin{pmatrix}
 158:  p-b+bq & \displaystyle\frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\\[5pt]
 159:  bq & s+b(1-q)
 160:  \end{pmatrix}.
 161:  \tag{F1}
 162: \]
 163: Here complete means that every \(L\in\mathcal K_2\) with the same stationary
 164: visible click law as \(K\) is \(K(q)\) for exactly one \(q\in I_\ast\).
 165: Writing \(T_0(\alpha,\eta)\) for the no-click kernel constructed with attempt
 166: rate \(\alpha\) and recovery rate \(\eta\), the endpoints are the two physical
 167: triangular kernels obtained by exchanging those rates:
 168: \[
 169:  K(1)=T_0(\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r}),
 170:  \qquad
 171:  K(q_\ast)=T_0(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Gamma).
 172:  \tag{F2}
 173: \]
 174: If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), every \(q\) strictly between the
 175: endpoints gives a strictly positive kernel with strictly positive killing
 176: deficits, and the physical triangular subfamily meets the arc only at the two
 177: endpoints.  If \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), then \(I_\ast=\{1\}\), so
 178: the entire two-state killed-reset fibre is a singleton.  Thus the unrestricted
 179: two-state hidden kernel is identifiable exactly on the exchange diagonal and
 180: has a continuum fibre off it; within the physical sampled-counter subfamily,
 181: the only ambiguity off the diagonal is the rate exchange.
 182: \end{theorem}
 183: 
 184: \begin{proof}
 185: First \(b>0\).  If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), direct evaluation of
 186: the defining integral gives
 187: \[
 188:  b=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
 189:  \qquad
 190:  b+s-p=\frac{\Gamma(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma}
 191:           =bq_\ast>0.
 192:  \tag{F3}
 193: \]
 194: The same identities hold by continuity on the diagonal, where
 195: \(p=s\), \(b=\Gamma\Delta\tau p>0\), and \(q_\ast=1\).  Consequently
 196: \[
 197:  \det[\mathbf1,K\mathbf1]=b+s-p=bq_\ast>0,
 198:  \qquad
 199:  \det\begin{bmatrix}e_2^\top\\e_2^\top K\end{bmatrix}=-b\ne0,
 200: \]
 201: so \(K\) is minimal.
 202: 
 203: Every member of \(\mathcal G_2\) has the unique form
 204: \[
 205:  M_q=\begin{pmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad q\ne0.
 206: \]
 207: Multiplication, using \(b+s-p=bq_\ast\), gives
 208: \(M_q^{-1}KM_q=K(q)\) in \textup{(F1)}.  Since \(K\) is minimal, its scalar
 209: Hankel sequence has rank two.  Any \(L\in\mathcal K_2\) with the same visible
 210: law has the same leading Hankel matrix; its factorization as
 211: \(\mathcal O(L)\mathcal C(L)\) has rank two, so both factors have rank two and
 212: \(L\) is minimal as well.  The recalled orbit--fibre proposition therefore
 213: forces every such \(L\) to have the displayed form.  If
 214: \(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2\), its lower-left entry
 215: is \(bq\ge0\).  Invertibility excludes \(q=0\), hence \(q>0\).  Its
 216: upper-right entry then yields the exact condition
 217: \[
 218:  \frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\ge0
 219:  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q\in I_\ast.
 220:  \tag{F4}
 221: \]
 222: 
 223: Conversely, let \(q\in I_\ast\).  The two diagonal entries in
 224: \textup{(F1)} are affine in \(q\), with endpoint values \(p,s\) and \(s,p\),
 225: respectively, and are therefore positive.  The lower-left entry is positive,
 226: and \textup{(F4)} makes the upper-right entry nonnegative.  Writing
 227: \(a=1-b-s>0\), the two killing deficits are
 228: \[
 229:  \mathbf1-K(q)\mathbf1
 230:  =\begin{pmatrix}a+bq_\ast/q\\a\end{pmatrix}>0.
 231:  \tag{F5}
 232: \]
 233: Similarity preserves the spectral radius
 234: \(\max\{p,s\}<1\), so \(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2\).  This proves that the
 235: displayed arc is the complete fibre.  It is injective because its lower-left
 236: entry is \(bq\).
 237: 
 238: At \(q=1\) one recovers \(K\).  At \(q=q_\ast\),
 239: \[
 240:  K(q_\ast)=\begin{pmatrix}s&0\\bq_\ast&p\end{pmatrix}.
 241: \]
 242: Equation~\textup{(F3)} says that \(bq_\ast\) is precisely the no-click
 243: recovery-to-ready probability after exchanging the two rates, and its second
 244: row has the same killing deficit \(a\); this proves \textup{(F2)}.  If
 245: \(q_\ast\ne1\), the product in the upper-right entry is strictly positive
 246: inside \(I_\ast\) and vanishes only at its endpoints.  All remaining entries
 247: and both deficits are already strict there.  If \(q_\ast=1\),
 248: \textup{(F4)} forces \(q=1\).  The endpoint, triangular-intersection, and
 249: identifiability statements follow.
 250: \end{proof}

  21: \paragraph{Recalled minimal-realization uniqueness.}
  22: Let \((a,A,b)\) and \((\widetilde a,\widetilde A,\widetilde b)\) be two real

  25: aA^k b=\widetilde a\widetilde A^k\widetilde b

  93: \[
  94: \mathfrak F_{\mathcal C}(K)=
  95: \left\{M^{-1}KM\in\mathcal C:M\in\mathcal G_n\right\}
  96: \big/\!\sim_{\mathcal C}.
  97: \]
  98: Then standard minimal-realization uniqueness gives the following exact
  99: characterization.
 100: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 101: \item Two minimal kernels \(K,L\in\mathcal K_n\) generate the same stationary
 102: visible click law if and only if
 103: \[
 104: \begin{aligned}
 105: L&=M^{-1}KM &&\text{for the unique }M\in\mathcal G_n\\
 106: &&&\text{implementing their normalized minimal realizations}.
 107: \end{aligned}
 108: \]
 109: \item Equivalently, the declared hidden object is identifiable from the visible law within
 110: \(\mathcal C\), modulo \(\sim_{\mathcal C}\), if and only if
 111: \[
 112: \#\mathfrak F_{\mathcal C}(K)=1\qquad\text{for every }K\in\mathcal C.
 113: \]
 114: Pointwise identifiability at \(K\) is equivalent to the same condition at
 115: that \(K\); if the cardinality exceeds one, its distinct classes are exactly
 116: the hidden nonidentifiability fibre. Thus this assertion is the orbit-fibre
 117: reformulation of part \textup{(i)}.
 118: \end{enumerate}
 119: Part~\textup{(ii)} is deliberately recorded only as terminology: after the
 120: fibre has been defined, singleton fibre and identifiability modulo
 121: \(\sim_{\mathcal C}\) are the same assertion.  Neither part is claimed as a
 122: new realization theorem.
 123: \end{proposition}
 124: 
 125: \begin{proof}
 126: Deterministic reset makes the visible process renewal. Its Palm gap tail is
 127: exactly \(S_k(K)\), so equality of visible stationary laws is equivalent to
 128: equality of all the scalar coordinates \(\beta K^k\mathbf1\), \(k\ge0\).
 129: Apply the minimal-realization theorem stated above to the triples
 130: \((\beta,K,\mathbf1)\) and \((\beta,L,\mathbf1)\). Its hypotheses are exactly
 131: the two displayed rank conditions in the proposition, and it gives a unique
 132: similarity \(L=M^{-1}KM\). Preservation of the fixed input and output vectors
 133: gives \(M\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) and \(\beta M=\beta\), respectively.
 134: Conversely, these two identities give
 135: \[
 136: \beta(M^{-1}KM)^k\mathbf1=\beta K^k\mathbf1
 137: \]
 138: for every \(k\), proving (i). Taking the intersection with
 139: \(\mathcal C\) and then quotienting precisely the declared structural
 140: equivalence proves
 141: the necessary-and-sufficient assertion (ii).
 142: \end{proof}

 252: \begin{corollary}[All-collision serial identifiability]
 253: \label{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main}
 254: Fix \(n\ge2\), a known \(\Delta\tau>0\), and arbitrary positive rates
 255: \(\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n)\), with repetitions allowed. Let
 256: \[
 257: Q(\theta)_{ii}=-\theta_i,\qquad
 258: Q(\theta)_{i,i-1}=\theta_i\quad(2\le i\le n),
 259: \]
 260: with all other entries zero, and put
 261: \[
 262: T_0(\theta)=e^{\Delta\tau Q(\theta)},\qquad
 263: T_1(\theta)=(I-T_0(\theta))\mathbf1e_n^\top.
 264: \]
 265: Then the visible record identifies exactly the unordered rate multiset
 266: \(\{\!\{\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n\}\!\}\). Equivalently, the fibre of the
 267: labelled serial parameter is its \(\mathfrak S_n\)-permutation orbit.
 268: 
 269: More explicitly, if the distinct rates are
 270: \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r\) with multiplicities
 271: \(m_1,\ldots,m_r\), and \(z_j=e^{-\lambda_j\Delta\tau}\), then the Palm tail
 272: has the confluent Prony form
 273: \[
 274: S_k=\sum_{j=1}^r\sum_{\ell=0}^{m_j-1}
 275: c_{j\ell}k^\ell z_j^k,\qquad c_{j,m_j-1}\ne0,
 276: \]
 277: and its minimal recurrence polynomial is
 278: \[
 279: \chi_\theta(x)=\prod_{j=1}^r(x-z_j)^{m_j}.
 280: \]
 281: The leading \(n\times n\) Hankel matrix
 282: \((S_{i+j})_{0\le i,j<n}\) is invertible; hence
 283: \(S_0,\ldots,S_{2n-1}\) determine \(\chi_\theta\), including all collision
 284: multiplicities. Pole collision therefore changes conditioning and the local
 285: root chart, but does not change population identifiability.
 286: \end{corollary}
 287: 
 288: \begin{proof}
 289: Starting in phase \(n\), the absorption time is
 290: \(W=X_n+\cdots+X_1\), where the \(X_i\) are independent exponentials with
 291: rates \(\theta_i\). Its Laplace transform is
 292: \[
 293: \EE e^{-sW}=\prod_{i=1}^n\frac{\theta_i}{s+\theta_i}.
 294: \]
 295: Consequently
 296: \[
 297: \int_0^\infty e^{-st}\PP(W>t)\,dt
 298: =\frac{1-\prod_{i=1}^n\theta_i/(s+\theta_i)}{s}
 299: \]
 300: has at
 301: \(-\lambda_j\) a pole of exact order \(m_j\). Partial-fraction inversion and
 302: sampling at \(t=k\Delta\tau\) give the displayed exponential-polynomial form
 303: with nonzero top confluent coefficient. Standard confluent Prony algebra
 304: then gives the exact minimal annihilator \(\chi_\theta\)
 305: \cite{KunisRoemerVonDerOhe2020Prony}.
 306: 
 307: For completeness of the finite-coordinate assertion, the matrices
 308: \(\mathcal O(Q)\) and \(\mathcal C(Q)\) are nonsingular: successive rows
 309: \(e_n^\top Q^j\) and successive columns \(Q^j\mathbf1\) expose the nonzero
 310: bidiagonal products triangularly. Because the exponential is injective on
 311: the real spectrum of \(Q\), Hermite interpolation supplies a polynomial
 312: \(p\) with \(Q=p(e^{\Delta\tau Q})\); hence the corresponding observation and
 313: reachability spaces for \(T_0=e^{\Delta\tau Q}\) are also full. Therefore
 314: \[
 315: (S_{i+j})_{0\le i,j<n}=\mathcal O(T_0)\mathcal C(T_0)
 316: \]
 317: is invertible, and the first \(2n\) tails solve uniquely for the order-\(n\)
 318: recurrence. The roots and their algebraic multiplicities recover
 319: \(\lambda_j=-\Delta\tau^{-1}\log z_j\) and \(m_j\). Conversely, permuting
 320: the independent summands does not change \(W\), the Palm gap law, or the
 321: stationary renewal law. This proves the exact fibre claim.
 322: \end{proof}

 324: \begin{theorem}[Quantitative interior fibre dimension and positivity persistence]
 325: \label{thm:nstate-interior-continuum-nonidentifiability-main}
 326: For the unrestricted class with \(\sim_{\mathcal K_n}\) equal to
 327: reset-preserving state relabelling, the hidden kernel is locally
 328: nonidentifiable at every minimal interior point \(K\), where interior means
 329: \(K>0\) and \((I-K)\mathbf1>0\) entrywise. More precisely, the
 330: reset-preserving similarity group has Lie algebra
 331: \[
 332: \mathfrak g_n=\{B:B\mathbf1=0,\ \beta B=0\},
 333: \qquad \dim\mathfrak g_n=(n-1)^2,
 334: \]
 335: and the orbit map
 336: \[
 337: \psi_K:\mathcal G_n\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{n\times n},\qquad
 338: \psi_K(M)=M^{-1}KM,
 339: \]
 340: has injective differential
 341: \[
 342: D\psi_K(I)B=[K,B]\qquad(B\in\mathfrak g_n).
 343: \]
 344: Consequently the visible fibre through \(K\) contains, in a neighbourhood of
 345: \(K\), a smooth immersed manifold of dimension exactly \((n-1)^2\).  Every
 346: kernel on a sufficiently small neighbourhood of this orbit manifold remains
 347: strictly substochastic: its entries and killing deficits are positive.  After
 348: quotienting by the finite reset-preserving permutation group, the local fibre
 349: still has dimension \((n-1)^2\).
 350: \end{theorem}
 351: 
 352: \begin{proof}
 353: Because \(\beta\mathbf1=1\),
 354: \(\RR^n=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\oplus\ker\beta\).  Relative to this
 355: decomposition, \(B\mathbf1=0\) removes the first block column and
 356: \(\beta B=0\) forces the range into \(\ker\beta\).  Thus
 357: \(B=\operatorname{diag}(0,A)\), with arbitrary
 358: \(A\in\operatorname{End}(\ker\beta)\), and
 359: \(\dim\mathfrak g_n=(n-1)^2\).
 360: 
 361: Differentiating \(\exp(-tB)K\exp(tB)\) at zero gives
 362: \(D\psi_K(I)B=[K,B]\).  Suppose \([K,B]=0\).  Since \(B\mathbf1=0\),
 363: \[
 364: BK^j\mathbf1=K^jB\mathbf1=0,
 365: \qquad j=0,\ldots,n-1.
 366: \]
 367: The reachability matrix
 368: \([\mathbf1,K\mathbf1,\ldots,K^{n-1}\mathbf1]\) has rank \(n\), so these
 369: equalities imply \(B=0\).  Hence the differential is injective on all of
 370: \(\mathfrak g_n\), not merely in one selected direction.
 371: 
 372: The constant-rank theorem now makes the image of \(\psi_K\) near the identity
 373: a smooth immersed manifold of dimension \((n-1)^2\).  For every
 374: \(M\in\mathcal G_n\),
 375: \[
 376: \beta\psi_K(M)^j\mathbf1=\beta K^j\mathbf1\qquad(j\ge0),
 377: \]
 378: so the recalled orbit-fibre result places this entire manifold in the visible
 379: fibre.  Finally, all entries of \(M^{-1}KM\) and all components of
 380: \((I-M^{-1}KM)\mathbf1\) depend continuously on \(M\).  Their values at
 381: \(M=I\) are strictly positive; a sufficiently small identity neighbourhood
 382: therefore remains inside the interior Markovian cone.  The stabilizer has zero
 383: Lie algebra by injectivity of the differential, and quotienting by the finite
 384: reset-preserving permutation group cannot change local dimension.  This proves
 385: all assertions.
 386: \end{proof}
 387: 
 388: \begin{remark}[Nonminimal and graph-specific open interfaces]
 389: \label{rem:nstate-identifiability-open-interfaces-main}
 390: The characterization and the two headline results deliberately assume
 391: Hankel/minimal rank \(n\). If a nominal
 392: \(n\)-state representation has lower visible rank, equal laws need not be
 393: related by an invertible \(n\times n\) similarity; a sharp classification then
 394: requires a stratified treatment of nonminimal augmentations. For a fixed
 395: nonserial zero pattern on the boundary of the Markovian cone, evaluating the
 396: orbit intersection \(\mathfrak F_{\mathcal C}(K)\) is an exact semialgebraic
 397: problem, but no graph-uniform closed form is claimed here. Finally, collision
 398: multiplicity is population-identifiable in the serial model but statistically
 399: singular under noisy finite records. These are explicit interfaces, not
 400: consequences of the present results.
 401: \end{remark}
 402: 
 403: For orientation, the unrestricted fibre is already nontrivial in two states:
 404: \[
 405: K=\begin{pmatrix}1/2&0\\1/2&1/4\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 406: M=\begin{pmatrix}9/10&1/10\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 407: M^{-1}KM=\begin{pmatrix}9/20&1/45\\9/20&3/10\end{pmatrix}.
 408: \]
 409: Both kernels are nonnegative and substochastic,
 410: \(M\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), \(e_2^\top M=e_2^\top\), and their entire visible
 411: renewal laws coincide, although the hidden kernels do not.

2830: \section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}
2831: 
2832: The paper gives a closed-form record-law and fixed-setting asymptotic analysis
2833: for one constrained latched killed-leakage sampled-counter D-MAP(2) subfamily.
2834: The visible
2835: record identifies the unordered survival/rate coordinates, not hidden labels
2836: or response-side thermodynamic parameters without external calibration.  The
2837: two-state fibre theorem makes this ambiguity exact in the larger killed-reset
2838: class: separated rates generate a closed continuum arc whose only triangular
2839: members are the two physical rate orderings, while equal rates generate a
2840: singleton fibre.  The diagonal statement is deliberately narrow: it is only
2841: the pointwise projected

2843: certificate, and it carries no confidence-procedure interpretation.

2849: \section{Related Work and Mathematical Comparison}\label{sec:theorem-led-comparison}
2850: 
2851: The introduction gives the mathematical narrative comparison with the closest
2852: renewal-binary, weak-memory, waiting-time, partial-observation, and detector
2853: papers.  This final section gives a compact theorem-by-theorem comparison with
2854: the direct D-MAP, MAP, and discrete phase-type literature, followed by the
2855: closest detector-model comparator.  Extended comparator tables and the search
2856: ledger are placed in the supplementary material.
2857: 
2858: \subsection{Detector dead-time comparator}\label{subsec:detector-dead-time-comparator-main}
2859: 
2860: In the nonparalyzable continuous dead-time model, an accepted event is followed
2861: by a fixed or random inactive period and then by a live waiting time; this
2862: structure produces renewal count statistics and motivates classical
2863: dead-time corrections and detector checks
2864: \cite{YuFessler2000,SarbaziSafariHaas2018LongDeadTime,
2865: GronbergDanielssonSjolin2018Nonparalyzable,MeeksSiegel2008DeadTime}.
2866: Krause--Walenta's continuous exponential-recovery model for free-running SPADs
2867: allows detection efficiency to recover continuously after dead time and fits
2868: parameters from inter-detection intervals \cite{KrauseWalenta2025SPADRecovery}.
2869: Such a detector need not have \(T_1(\cdot,R)=0\): after a click, physical
2870: recovery and further evolution can occur before the next externally chosen bin
2871: boundary.  In contrast, the present model is a sampled discrete D-MAP with
2872: stochastic recovery before a click and an explicit post-click latch until the
2873: boundary.
2874: Its Palm zero-run law is
2875: \[
2876: g_k=e_D^\top T_0^kT_1\mathbf1
2877: =\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(1-p)p^k-\Gamma(1-s)s^k}
2878:        {\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
2879: \]
2880: with the continuous equal-rate limit understood.  The contribution relative to
2881: the detector dead-time literature is therefore not a generic dead-time
2882: correction.  It is an exact quotient inverse for the sampled killed-leakage
2883: D-MAP visible law, together with the renewal product and retained-record
2884: covariance route that are valid only under the boundary-reset convention in
2885: \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main,prop:model-fragility-boundary-reset-main}.
2886: 
2887: \subsection{Theorem-by-theorem comparison with DMAP, DPH, and MAP theory}
2888: 
2889: \paragraph{Theorem A (record law).}
2890: Alfa--Neuts supply the general D-MAP construction
2891: \cite{AlfaNeuts1995DMAP}, while M\'esz\'aros--Telek study canonical
2892: representations for general discrete order-two MAPs and RAPs
2893: \cite{MeszarosTelek2013DiscreteMAP2Canonical}.  Those representation results
2894: do not assert that the present triangular, deterministically reset subfamily is
2895: renewal.  The additional calculation here is restricted to that subfamily: it
2896: derives the Palm gap law, increasing hazard, one-mode covariance, and exact
2897: \(1\)-dependence criterion.  These are elementary model-specific consequences,
2898: not a new general DMAP theorem.
2899: 
2900: \paragraph{Theorem B (three-inclusion quotient inverse).}
2901: The closest prior result is the canonical-coordinate analysis of discrete
2902: order-two MAP/RAP models by M\'esz\'aros--Telek
2903: \cite{MeszarosTelek2013DiscreteMAP2Canonical}, together with canonical MAP2
2904: and matrix-exponential representation work
2905: \cite{BodrogHeindlHorvathTelek2008MAP2Canonical,
2906: TelekHorvath2007MinimalMAP}.  That literature constructs sparse or canonical
2907: representatives and moment-matching maps for broader representation classes.
2908: Theorem~B neither replaces nor strengthens those canonical-form theorems.  Its
2909: narrow additional statement is the direct rational identity
2910: \[
2911: \frac{r_2-r_0^2}{r_1-r_0^2}=p-b
2912: \]
2913: for the latched killed-reset image, which converts three visible binary
2914: inclusion probabilities into \((p+s,ps)\) and hence the complete visible
2915: renewal law.  The estimand is a law-determining quotient, not a labelled
2916: minimal DMAP2 representative.  We do not claim that this identity is absent as
2917: an implicit specialization of canonical DMAP2 coordinates; the contribution
2918: is the explicit three-inclusion specialization and its stability bounds.
2919: 
2920: \paragraph{Theorems C and D (asymptotics).}
2921: The regenerative CLT, separated-batch method, and multivariate delta method are
2922: standard inputs \cite{Zamparo2022RenewalBinary,Janson2024RenewalCLT,
2923: AsmussenGlynn2007,FlegalJones2010BatchMeansSpectral}.  The paper's additional
2924: work is bookkeeping for complete retained cycles, the explicit stopped-prefix
2925: bounds, and transport to the three-inclusion quotient.  The sorted-root and
2926: log-rate CLTs are direct delta-method consequences and are not claimed as new
2927: asymptotic theory.
2928: 
2929: \paragraph{Theorem E (projection example).}
2930: Metric-projection limits at smooth inequality boundaries are standard
2931: \cite{Shapiro1987MetricProjection,FangSeo2021ProjectionTests}.  Theorem~E is
2932: therefore presented only as a pointwise worked projection at \(z_0=1/2\), with
2933: a reproducible covariance nondegeneracy certificate.  It makes no inferential
2934: or novelty claim beyond this specialization.
2935: 
2936: \paragraph{Complete-law checking and the Markov--Palm score.}
2937: Distributional-distance consistency, serial-independence basis tests,
2938: finite-range and Hilbert-space central limit theorems, and local Gaussian
2939: shift calculus are standard inputs
2940: \cite{RyabkoRyabko2010ErgodicInference,Ryabko2012StationaryTesting,
2941: SkaugTjostheim1993SerialIndependence,DedeckerMerlevede2003HilbertCLT,
2942: vanDerVaart1998AsymptoticStatistics}.
2943: \Cref{thm:complete-visible-law-specification-main} combines those inputs with
2944: the sampled-counter word law and an explicit rank-one Markov-gap path.  The
2945: model-specific extension in
2946: \Cref{thm:complete-markov-palm-tangent-omnibus-main} is the exact closed
2947: interaction space obtained by adding $q(0,0)=0$ to double centring, its
2948: $\mu^{-1}$-scaled efficient projection, and the exchange-boundary calibration
2949: of a trace-weighted score.  It claims pointwise strict local power in every
2950: nonzero interaction direction, but neither a new general independence test
2951: nor a uniform infinite-dimensional minimax envelope.
2952: 
2953: The growing-dimensional coupling invoked for the Helmert truncation is likewise
2954: external: CMU's Corollaries~2.2--2.3 supply the
2955: martingale and independent-vector Yurinskii bounds
2956: \cite{CattaneoMasiniUnderwood2025Yurinskii}.  The model-specific calculation
2957: checks their inputs.  Because those bounds retain an ambient-dimension factor,
2958: \Cref{prop:helmert-growing-layer-bracket-main} states only the proved
2959: necessary/sufficient bracket and leaves its logarithmic gap open.
2960: 
2961: \paragraph{Fibre results.}
2962: Minimal-realization uniqueness is classical, beginning with Kalman and used
2963: directly for MAP reduction and moment matching by Telek--Horv\'ath
2964: \cite{Kalman1963LinearSystems,TelekHorvath2007MinimalMAP}.  Accordingly,
2965: \Cref{thm:nstate-killed-reset-identifiability-dichotomy-main} is explicitly a
2966: recalled orbit-fibre reformulation.  The new two-state assertion is
2967: \Cref{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main}: for the physical triangular
2968: kernel, the complete Markovian orbit intersection is an explicit closed arc
2969: between the rate-swapped endpoints and collapses exactly on the exchange
2970: diagonal.  General MAP2 nonidentifiability and weak-equivalence results are the
2971: nearest representation-theoretic comparators
2972: \cite{RamirezCoboLilloWiper2010MAP2Nonidentifiability,
2973: RamirezCoboLillo2012WeakEquivalentMAP}; the claim here is only this exact
2974: killed-reset sampled-counter specialization.
2975: 
2976: The further new assertion is
2977: \Cref{thm:nstate-interior-continuum-nonidentifiability-main}: the unrestricted
2978: interior fibre contains a positivity-preserving similarity manifold of exact
2979: dimension \((n-1)^2\).  For serial kernels, Cumani's canonical failure-time
2980: forms, acyclic DPH estimation, and order-two/three discrete PH canonical forms
2981: are direct predecessors
2982: \cite{Cumani1982CanonicalFailure,BobbioEtAl2003AcyclicDPH,
2983: PappTelek2013DiscretePHCanonical,MeszarosPappTelek2014Traffic}.
2984: \Cref{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main} is consequently
2985: stated as a killed-reset orbit-intersection calculation: the pure serial fibre
2986: is exactly the rate-multiset permutation class, with collisions handled by the
2987: confluent recurrence.  It is not claimed as a new general acyclic-DPH
2988: canonical-form theorem.  General phase-type nonuniqueness remains fully
2989: consistent with O'Cinneide's invariant-polytope analysis
2990: \cite{OCinneide1989PhaseTypeNonuniqueness,OCinneide1991InvariantPolytopes}.

"""Numerical feasibility checks for killed-reset D-MAP identifiability.

The serial model has a transient continuous-time generator with successive
rates ``rates``.  Sampling it at unit time gives T0=exp(Q); absorption is a
click and deterministically resets the next hidden state to the last phase,
so T1=(I-T0)1 e_n^T.  Its visible record is renewal.

This script checks six different questions that must not be conflated:

1. In the serial subclass, do visible coordinates recover the unordered rate
   multiset, including pole collisions?  A Hankel recurrence applied to the
   Palm gap-tail sequence recovers the sampled poles exp(-rate_i), with their
   algebraic multiplicities, for representative n=2,3,4 examples.
2. Does killed reset alone identify a hidden kernel?  No.  A stochastic
   similarity transform gives a different nonnegative killed-reset kernel
   with exactly the same visible renewal law.
3. Does a physical two-state inclusion triple satisfy the exact scalar image
   equation?  The residual is checked on separated and repeated-rate examples.
4. Does the hidden mode obey its sharp global secant-slope bound?
5. Does the exact mean sampled cycle have the stated small-interval expansion?
6. What is the complete Markovian similarity fibre of the physical two-state
   kernel?  The exact arc parameter runs between 1 and gamma/recovery; its
   endpoints are the rate-swapped physical kernels, while its interior is
   strictly positive and has the same complete Palm tail.

The numerical searches are evidence and diagnostics, not proofs of global
injectivity.  The associated manuscript theorem supplies the exact minimal
similarity-orbit criterion and proves serial identifiability for arbitrary
positive rates, including collision strata.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np
from numpy.typing import ArrayLike, NDArray
from scipy.linalg import eig, expm
from scipy.optimize import least_squares
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree


FloatArray = NDArray[np.float64]


def hidden_mode_secant(x: float, y: float) -> float:
    """Return the secant slope of t*exp(-t), with its diagonal limit."""
    if not np.isfinite(x) or not np.isfinite(y) or min(x, y) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("x and y must be finite and positive")
    if x == y:
        return float(np.exp(-x) * (1.0 - x))
    return float((y * np.exp(-y) - x * np.exp(-x)) / (y - x))


def symmetric_log_divided_difference(p: float, s: float) -> float:
    """Return the symmetric logarithmic divided difference C(p,s)."""
    if not np.isfinite(p) or not np.isfinite(s) or min(p, s) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("p and s must be finite and positive")
    midpoint = 0.5 * (p + s)
    half_gap = 0.5 * (p - s)
    if abs(half_gap) <= 1e-6 * midpoint:
        log_midpoint = np.log(midpoint)
        return float(
            midpoint * (1.0 - log_midpoint)
            + half_gap**2 / midpoint * (0.5 + log_midpoint / 3.0)
            + half_gap**4 / midpoint**3 * (1.0 / 12.0 + 4.0 * log_midpoint / 45.0)
        )
    return float((s * np.log(p) - p * np.log(s)) / (np.log(p) - np.log(s)))


def two_state_inclusion_coordinates(
    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
) -> FloatArray:
    """Return (r0,r1,r2) for the physical two-state sampled counter."""
    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
    x = gamma * delta
    y = recovery * delta
    p = float(np.exp(-x))
    s = float(np.exp(-y))
    if x == y:
        b = x * p
    else:
        b = y * (p - s) / (y - x)
    a = 1.0 - s - b
    rho = (1.0 - p) * (1.0 - s) / (1.0 - p + b)
    hidden_lambda = p - b
    r1 = rho * a
    r2 = rho * rho + hidden_lambda * (r1 - rho * rho)
    return np.array([rho, r1, r2])


def sampled_counter_killed_kernel(
    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
) -> FloatArray:
    """Return the physical two-state no-click kernel."""
    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery, delta))):
        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be finite")
    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
    p = float(np.exp(-gamma * delta))
    s = float(np.exp(-recovery * delta))
    difference = recovery - gamma
    if difference == 0.0:
        b = recovery * delta * p
    else:
        b = recovery * p * (-np.expm1(-difference * delta)) / difference
    return np.array([[p, 0.0], [b, s]])


def sampled_counter_fibre_interval(
    gamma: float, recovery: float
) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Return the exact closed q-interval of Markovian similarity equivalents."""
    finite_rates = np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery)))
    if not finite_rates or min(gamma, recovery) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("rates must be finite and positive")
    endpoint = gamma / recovery
    return min(1.0, endpoint), max(1.0, endpoint)


def sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(
    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float, q: float
) -> FloatArray:
    """Return the q member of the exact physical two-state Markovian fibre."""
    if not np.isfinite(q):
        raise ValueError("q must be finite")
    lower, upper = sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
    if q < lower or q > upper:
        raise ValueError("q lies outside the exact Markovian fibre interval")
    physical = sampled_counter_killed_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta)
    p = float(physical[0, 0])
    b = float(physical[1, 0])
    s = float(physical[1, 1])
    endpoint = gamma / recovery
    equivalent = np.array(
        [
            [p - b + b * q, b * (1.0 - q) * (q - endpoint) / q],
            [b * q, s + b * (1.0 - q)],
        ]
    )
    deficits = np.ones(2) - equivalent @ np.ones(2)
    if float(equivalent.min()) < -1e-12 or float(deficits.min()) < -1e-12:
        raise ArithmeticError("closed-form fibre member is not substochastic")
    return equivalent


def physical_image_residual(inclusions: ArrayLike) -> float:
    """Evaluate the exact three-inclusion sampled-counter image equation."""
    coordinates = np.asarray(inclusions, dtype=float)
    if coordinates.size != 3:
        raise ValueError("exactly r0, r1, and r2 are required")
    r0, r1, r2 = coordinates
    denominator = r1 - r0 * r0
    if r0 <= 0.0 or denominator == 0.0:
        raise ValueError("the inclusion triple is outside the stable inverse chart")
    a = r1 / r0
    hidden_lambda = (r2 - r0 * r0) / denominator
    sigma1 = 1.0 - a + hidden_lambda
    sigma2 = r0 * (1.0 - hidden_lambda) - a + hidden_lambda
    discriminant = sigma1 * sigma1 - 4.0 * sigma2
    if discriminant < -1e-13:
        raise ValueError("the quotient polynomial has nonreal roots")
    root_gap = np.sqrt(max(discriminant, 0.0))
    p = 0.5 * (sigma1 + root_gap)
    s = 0.5 * (sigma1 - root_gap)
    return float(a - 1.0 + symmetric_log_divided_difference(p, s))


def mean_cycle_length(gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float) -> float:
    """Return E(G+1) for the two-stage sampled cycle."""
    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
    x = gamma * delta
    y = recovery * delta
    gx = 1.0 / (-np.expm1(-x))
    if x == y:
        return float(gx + x * np.exp(-x) * gx * gx)
    gy = 1.0 / (-np.expm1(-y))
    return float((y * gx - x * gy) / (y - x))


def small_delta_mean_expansion(
    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
) -> float:
    """Return the expansion of delta*E(G+1) through order delta^4."""
    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
    return float(
        1.0 / gamma
        + 1.0 / recovery
        + delta / 2.0
        + gamma * recovery * (gamma + recovery) * delta**4 / 720.0
    )


def serial_generator(rates: ArrayLike) -> FloatArray:
    """Return the lower-bidiagonal transient generator for serial phases."""
    rate_array = np.asarray(rates, dtype=float)
    if rate_array.ndim != 1 or rate_array.size < 2:
        raise ValueError("rates must be a one-dimensional tuple of length at least two")
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(rate_array)) or np.any(rate_array <= 0.0):
        raise ValueError("all rates must be finite and positive")
    generator = np.diag(-rate_array)
    for index in range(1, rate_array.size):
        generator[index, index - 1] = rate_array[index]
    return generator


def serial_killed_reset_kernels(
    rates: ArrayLike, delta: float = 1.0
) -> tuple[FloatArray, FloatArray]:
    """Construct the serial killed-reset D-MAP kernels T0 and T1."""
    if not np.isfinite(delta) or delta <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("delta must be finite and positive")
    t0 = expm(delta * serial_generator(rates))
    n_states = t0.shape[0]
    reset = np.zeros(n_states)
    reset[-1] = 1.0
    click_probability = np.ones(n_states) - t0 @ np.ones(n_states)
    t1 = np.outer(click_probability, reset)
    if min(float(t0.min()), float(t1.min())) < -1e-12:
        raise ArithmeticError("matrix exponential did not produce nonnegative kernels")
    return t0, t1


def kernel_tail_coordinates(t0: ArrayLike, count: int) -> FloatArray:
    """Return S_k=e_n^T T0^k 1 for k=0,...,count-1."""
    matrix = np.asarray(t0, dtype=float)
    if matrix.ndim != 2 or matrix.shape[0] != matrix.shape[1]:
        raise ValueError("t0 must be square")
    if count < 1:
        raise ValueError("count must be positive")
    alpha = np.zeros(matrix.shape[0])
    alpha[-1] = 1.0
    ones = np.ones(matrix.shape[0])
    power = np.eye(matrix.shape[0])
    tails = np.empty(count)
    for lag in range(count):
        tails[lag] = alpha @ power @ ones
        power = power @ matrix
    return tails


def visible_tail_coordinates(
    rates: ArrayLike, count: int, delta: float = 1.0
) -> FloatArray:
    """Return visible Palm zero-run tails for a serial rate tuple."""
    t0, _ = serial_killed_reset_kernels(rates, delta)
    return kernel_tail_coordinates(t0, count)


def recover_sampled_poles(tails: ArrayLike, n_states: int) -> FloatArray:
    """Recover the unordered poles from a square Hankel matrix pencil."""
    tail_array = np.asarray(tails, dtype=float)
    if tail_array.size < 2 * n_states:
        raise ValueError("the n-state pencil needs S_0 through S_{2n-1}")
    h0 = np.array(
        [[tail_array[row + col] for col in range(n_states)] for row in range(n_states)]
    )
    h1 = np.array(
        [
            [tail_array[row + col + 1] for col in range(n_states)]
            for row in range(n_states)
        ]
    )
    poles = eig(h1, h0, right=False)
    if np.max(np.abs(poles.imag)) > 1e-8:
        raise ArithmeticError("recovered poles are not numerically real")
    real_poles = np.sort(poles.real)
    if np.any(real_poles <= 0.0) or np.any(real_poles >= 1.0):
        raise ArithmeticError("recovered poles are outside (0,1)")
    return real_poles


def visible_click_moments(
    rates: ArrayLike, max_lag: int, delta: float = 1.0
) -> FloatArray:
    """Return E[A_0] and E[A_0 A_l] for l=1,...,max_lag."""
    if max_lag < 0:
        raise ValueError("max_lag must be nonnegative")
    t0, _ = serial_killed_reset_kernels(rates, delta)
    n_states = t0.shape[0]
    alpha = np.zeros(n_states)
    alpha[-1] = 1.0
    ones = np.ones(n_states)
    rho = 1.0 / (alpha @ np.linalg.solve(np.eye(n_states) - t0, ones))
    tails = kernel_tail_coordinates(t0, max_lag + 1)
    interarrival = np.zeros(max_lag + 1)
    for lag in range(1, max_lag + 1):
        interarrival[lag] = tails[lag - 1] - tails[lag]
    renewal_mass = np.zeros(max_lag + 1)
    renewal_mass[0] = 1.0
    for lag in range(1, max_lag + 1):
        renewal_mass[lag] = sum(
            interarrival[jump] * renewal_mass[lag - jump]
            for jump in range(1, lag + 1)
        )
    return rho * renewal_mass


def recover_two_state_rates_from_three_inclusions(
    moments: ArrayLike, delta: float = 1.0
) -> FloatArray:
    """Apply the paper's existing n=2 three-inclusion quotient inverse."""
    coordinates = np.asarray(moments, dtype=float)
    if coordinates.size < 3:
        raise ValueError("r0, r1, and r2 are required")
    rho, r1, r2 = coordinates[:3]
    a = r1 / rho
    u2 = r2 / rho
    hidden_lambda = (u2 - rho) / (a - rho)
    pole_sum = 1.0 - a + hidden_lambda
    pole_product = rho * (1.0 - hidden_lambda) - a + hidden_lambda
    poles = np.sort(np.roots([1.0, -pole_sum, pole_product]).real)
    return np.sort(-np.log(poles) / delta)


def equivalent_killed_reset_kernel(t0: ArrayLike, epsilon: float) -> FloatArray:
    """Return a nontrivial stochastic-similarity equivalent killed kernel."""
    matrix = np.asarray(t0, dtype=float)
    n_states = matrix.shape[0]
    if matrix.ndim != 2 or matrix.shape[1] != n_states or n_states < 2:
        raise ValueError("t0 must be square with at least two states")
    transform = np.eye(n_states)
    transform[0, 0] = 1.0 - epsilon
    transform[0, 1] = epsilon
    equivalent = np.linalg.solve(transform, matrix @ transform)
    deficits = np.ones(n_states) - equivalent @ np.ones(n_states)
    if float(equivalent.min()) < -1e-12 or float(deficits.min()) < -1e-12:
        raise ValueError("epsilon does not preserve a nonnegative killed-reset kernel")
    return equivalent


def finite_difference_jacobian(rates: ArrayLike, max_lag: int) -> FloatArray:
    """Differentiate the visible click-moment map by centered differences."""
    rate_array = np.asarray(rates, dtype=float)
    jacobian = np.empty((max_lag + 1, rate_array.size))
    for column, rate in enumerate(rate_array):
        step = 1e-6 * max(1.0, rate)
        upper = rate_array.copy()
        lower = rate_array.copy()
        upper[column] += step
        lower[column] -= step
        jacobian[:, column] = (
            visible_click_moments(upper, max_lag)
            - visible_click_moments(lower, max_lag)
        ) / (2.0 * step)
    return jacobian


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SearchSummary:
    starts: int
    converged: int
    canonical_fibers: tuple[tuple[float, ...], ...]
    labelled_orders: tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]
    best_nonpermutation_residual: float


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HankelDiagnostics:
    rank: int
    determinant: float
    condition_number: float
    smallest_singular_value: float


def hankel_diagnostics(tails: ArrayLike, n_states: int) -> HankelDiagnostics:
    """Return numerical rank and conditioning of the leading Hankel block."""
    tail_array = np.asarray(tails, dtype=float)
    if tail_array.size < 2 * n_states - 1:
        raise ValueError("the Hankel block needs S_0 through S_{2n-2}")
    hankel = np.array(
        [[tail_array[row + col] for col in range(n_states)] for row in range(n_states)]
    )
    singular_values = np.linalg.svd(hankel, compute_uv=False)
    tolerance = singular_values[0] * max(hankel.shape) * np.finfo(float).eps
    return HankelDiagnostics(
        rank=int(np.sum(singular_values > tolerance)),
        determinant=float(np.linalg.det(hankel)),
        condition_number=float(singular_values[0] / singular_values[-1]),
        smallest_singular_value=float(singular_values[-1]),
    )


def recover_minimal_recurrence(
    tails: ArrayLike, n_states: int
) -> tuple[FloatArray, float]:
    """Recover the monic order-n annihilator and its tail residual.

    If ``p(x)=x^n+c_{n-1}x^(n-1)+...+c_0``, the returned coefficients are
    ``[1,c_{n-1},...,c_0]``.  Repeated roots retain their multiplicities.
    """
    tail_array = np.asarray(tails, dtype=float)
    if tail_array.size < 2 * n_states:
        raise ValueError("the recurrence needs S_0 through S_{2n-1}")
    h0 = np.array(
        [[tail_array[row + col] for col in range(n_states)] for row in range(n_states)]
    )
    future = np.array([tail_array[row + n_states] for row in range(n_states)])
    ascending = np.linalg.solve(h0, -future)
    polynomial = np.concatenate(([1.0], ascending[::-1]))
    residuals = []
    for offset in range(tail_array.size - n_states):
        residuals.append(
            tail_array[offset + n_states]
            + float(ascending @ tail_array[offset : offset + n_states])
        )
    return polynomial, float(np.max(np.abs(residuals)))


def reset_similarity_lie_basis(n_states: int) -> tuple[FloatArray, ...]:
    """Basis of B1=0 and e_n^T B=0, the reset-preserving similarity tangent."""
    if n_states < 2:
        raise ValueError("n_states must be at least two")
    basis = []
    for row in range(n_states - 1):
        for column in range(n_states - 1):
            tangent = np.zeros((n_states, n_states))
            tangent[row, column] = 1.0
            tangent[row, -1] = -1.0
            basis.append(tangent)
    return tuple(basis)


def multistart_fiber_search(
    target_rates: ArrayLike, starts: int, seed: int
) -> SearchSummary:
    """Search numerically for rate tuples sharing the target click moments."""
    target = np.asarray(target_rates, dtype=float)
    max_lag = 2 * target.size + 2
    target_moments = visible_click_moments(target, max_lag)
    scale = np.maximum(np.abs(target_moments), 1e-4)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    accepted: list[FloatArray] = []
    residuals: list[float] = []

    def residual(log_rates: FloatArray) -> FloatArray:
        return (visible_click_moments(np.exp(log_rates), max_lag) - target_moments) / scale

    for _ in range(starts):
        initial = rng.uniform(np.log(0.15), np.log(3.5), size=target.size)
        fit = least_squares(
            residual,
            initial,
            bounds=(np.log(0.08), np.log(5.0)),
            xtol=1e-12,
            ftol=1e-12,
            gtol=1e-12,
            max_nfev=2500,
        )
        norm = float(np.linalg.norm(residual(fit.x)))
        if norm < 1e-8:
            accepted.append(np.exp(fit.x))
            residuals.append(norm)

    canonical = sorted(
        {
            tuple(np.round(np.sort(solution), 4))
            for solution in accepted
        }
    )
    labelled_orders = sorted(
        {
            tuple(np.argsort(solution).tolist())
            for solution in accepted
        }
    )
    target_sorted = np.sort(target)
    nonpermutation = [
        residual_value
        for solution, residual_value in zip(accepted, residuals)
        if np.linalg.norm(np.sort(solution) - target_sorted) > 1e-3
    ]
    return SearchSummary(
        starts=starts,
        converged=len(accepted),
        canonical_fibers=tuple(canonical),
        labelled_orders=tuple(labelled_orders),
        best_nonpermutation_residual=min(nonpermutation, default=float("inf")),
    )


def random_nearest_pair_search(
    n_states: int, samples: int, seed: int
) -> tuple[float, float, tuple[float, ...], tuple[float, ...]]:
    """Find the closest sampled moment vectors among sorted random tuples."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    rates = np.sort(
        np.exp(rng.uniform(np.log(0.15), np.log(3.5), size=(samples, n_states))),
        axis=1,
    )
    moments = np.array([visible_click_moments(row, 2 * n_states + 2) for row in rates])
    scale = np.maximum(moments.std(axis=0), 1e-10)
    normalized = moments / scale
    distances, indices = cKDTree(normalized).query(normalized, k=2)
    index = int(np.argmin(distances[:, 1]))
    partner = int(indices[index, 1])
    moment_distance = float(np.linalg.norm(normalized[index] - normalized[partner]))
    rate_distance = float(np.linalg.norm(rates[index] - rates[partner]))
    return (
        moment_distance,
        rate_distance,
        tuple(rates[index]),
        tuple(rates[partner]),
    )


def array_string(values: ArrayLike) -> str:
    return np.array2string(
        np.asarray(values), precision=10, suppress_small=False, floatmode="fixed"
    )


def report_example(rates: tuple[float, ...], search_starts: int = 80) -> None:
    n_states = len(rates)
    t0, t1 = serial_killed_reset_kernels(rates)
    tails = kernel_tail_coordinates(t0, 2 * n_states)
    extended_tails = kernel_tail_coordinates(t0, 3 * n_states + 1)
    moments = visible_click_moments(rates, 2 * n_states + 2)
    recurrence, recurrence_residual = recover_minimal_recurrence(
        extended_tails, n_states
    )
    roots = np.roots(recurrence)
    recovered_rates = np.sort(-np.log(np.abs(roots)))
    diagnostics = hankel_diagnostics(tails, n_states)
    permutations = list(itertools.permutations(rates))
    permutation_error = max(
        float(np.max(np.abs(visible_click_moments(item, 2 * n_states + 2) - moments)))
        for item in permutations
    )
    singular_values = np.linalg.svd(
        finite_difference_jacobian(rates, 2 * n_states + 2), compute_uv=False
    )

    print(f"n={n_states} serial killed-reset example")
    print(f"rates={rates}")
    print("T0=")
    print(array_string(t0))
    print("T1=")
    print(array_string(t1))
    print(f"Palm tails S_0,...,S_{2 * n_states - 1}={array_string(tails)}")
    print(f"click moments r_0,...,r_{2 * n_states + 2}={array_string(moments)}")
    print(f"Hankel recurrence polynomial={array_string(recurrence)}")
    print(f"expected sampled-pole polynomial={array_string(np.poly(np.exp(-np.asarray(rates))))}")
    print(f"maximum recurrence residual={recurrence_residual:.3e}")
    print(
        "leading Hankel diagnostics: "
        f"rank={diagnostics.rank}, determinant={diagnostics.determinant:.3e}, "
        f"condition={diagnostics.condition_number:.3e}, "
        f"sigma_min={diagnostics.smallest_singular_value:.3e}"
    )
    print(f"recovered unordered rates (root moduli)={array_string(recovered_rates)}")
    if n_states == 2:
        print(
            "three-inclusion recovered unordered rates="
            f"{array_string(recover_two_state_rates_from_three_inclusions(moments))}"
        )
    print(f"maximum moment error over all labelled permutations={permutation_error:.3e}")
    print(f"moment-map Jacobian singular values={array_string(singular_values)}")

    search = multistart_fiber_search(rates, starts=search_starts, seed=100 + n_states)
    print(
        f"multistart search: {search.converged}/{search.starts} converged; "
        f"canonical sorted fibers={search.canonical_fibers}"
    )
    print(f"labelled permutation orders reached={search.labelled_orders}")
    if np.isfinite(search.best_nonpermutation_residual):
        print(
            "WARNING: accepted non-permutation solution with scaled residual="
            f"{search.best_nonpermutation_residual:.3e}"
        )
    else:
        print("no accepted non-permutation solution found")

    nearest = random_nearest_pair_search(n_states, samples=900, seed=200 + n_states)
    print(
        "random nearest-pair search: normalized moment distance="
        f"{nearest[0]:.3e}, rate distance={nearest[1]:.3e}"
    )
    print(f"nearest sorted tuples={nearest[2]} and {nearest[3]}")

    equivalent = equivalent_killed_reset_kernel(t0, epsilon=0.02)
    tail_difference = float(
        np.max(
            np.abs(
                kernel_tail_coordinates(t0, 20)
                - kernel_tail_coordinates(equivalent, 20)
            )
        )
    )
    print("non-serial stochastic-similarity equivalent T0'=")
    print(array_string(equivalent))
    print(f"||T0'-T0||_F={np.linalg.norm(equivalent - t0):.3e}")
    print(f"maximum S_0,...,S_19 difference={tail_difference:.3e}")
    print(f"reset-preserving similarity tangent dimension={(n_states - 1) ** 2}")
    print(
        "interpretation: killed reset alone has a nontrivial hidden-kernel "
        "fiber, while the serial rate tuple is recovered here only as an "
        "unordered multiset."
    )
    print()

import unittest

class SerialKilledLeakageTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_two_state_physical_fibre_endpoints_are_rate_swaps(self):
        gamma = 0.7
        recovery = 1.6
        delta = 0.8
        lower, upper = verify.sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
        endpoint_kernels = (
            verify.sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta, lower),
            verify.sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta, upper),
        )
        physical_endpoints = (
            verify.sampled_counter_killed_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta),
            verify.sampled_counter_killed_kernel(recovery, gamma, delta),
        )
        for expected in physical_endpoints:
            self.assertTrue(
                any(
                    np.allclose(actual, expected, atol=2e-13)
                    for actual in endpoint_kernels
                )
            )

    def test_two_state_physical_fibre_interior_is_positive_and_visible_equivalent(
        self,
    ):
        gamma = 2.1
        recovery = 0.9
        delta = 0.6
        lower, upper = verify.sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
        q = 0.35 * lower + 0.65 * upper
        baseline = verify.sampled_counter_killed_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta)
        interior = verify.sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta, q)
        self.assertGreater(float(interior.min()), 0.0)
        deficits = np.ones(2) - interior @ np.ones(2)
        self.assertGreater(float(deficits.min()), 0.0)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(
            verify.kernel_tail_coordinates(interior, 30),
            verify.kernel_tail_coordinates(baseline, 30),
            rtol=2e-12,
            atol=2e-13,
        )

    def test_two_state_physical_fibre_collapses_exactly_on_exchange_diagonal(
        self,
    ):
        lower, upper = verify.sampled_counter_fibre_interval(1.3, 1.3)
        self.assertEqual(lower, 1.0)
        self.assertEqual(upper, 1.0)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            verify.sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(1.3, 1.3, 0.7, 1.0 + 1e-5)

    def test_two_state_physical_fibre_rejects_points_beyond_exact_arc(self):
        gamma = 0.7
        recovery = 1.6
        lower, upper = verify.sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            verify.sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(gamma, recovery, 1.0, lower - 1e-6)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            verify.sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(gamma, recovery, 1.0, upper + 1e-6)

    def test_exact_three_inclusion_image_equation(self):
        examples = (
            (0.35, 0.8, 0.2),
            (0.7, 1.6, 1.0),
            (2.0, 2.0, 1.0),
            (4.0, 0.45, 0.7),
        )
        for gamma, recovery, delta in examples:
            inclusions = verify.two_state_inclusion_coordinates(
                gamma, recovery, delta
            )
            residual = verify.physical_image_residual(inclusions)
            self.assertLess(abs(residual), 2e-12)

    def test_physical_image_equation_detects_intensity_perturbation(self):
        inclusions = verify.two_state_inclusion_coordinates(0.7, 1.6, 1.0)
        perturbed = inclusions.copy()
        perturbed[0] *= 1.01
        self.assertGreater(abs(verify.physical_image_residual(perturbed)), 1e-4)

    def test_hidden_mode_obeys_sharp_global_bound(self):
        grid = np.geomspace(1e-4, 50.0, 181)
        values = np.array(
            [verify.hidden_mode_secant(x, y) for x in grid for y in grid]
        )
        self.assertGreaterEqual(float(values.min()), -np.exp(-2.0) - 2e-14)
        self.assertLess(float(values.max()), 1.0)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(
            verify.hidden_mode_secant(2.0, 2.0), -np.exp(-2.0), places=15
        )

    def test_small_sampling_interval_mean_expansion_has_sixth_order_remainder(self):
        gamma = 0.7
        recovery = 1.6
        normalized_errors = []
        for delta in (0.2, 0.1, 0.05):
            exact = delta * verify.mean_cycle_length(gamma, recovery, delta)
            approximation = verify.small_delta_mean_expansion(
                gamma, recovery, delta
            )
            normalized_errors.append(abs(exact - approximation) / delta**6)
        self.assertLess(max(normalized_errors), 2e-3)

    def test_kernels_are_stochastic_and_clicks_reset(self):
        for rates in ((0.7, 1.6), (0.7, 1.2, 2.3)):
            t0, t1 = verify.serial_killed_reset_kernels(rates)
            np.testing.assert_allclose((t0 + t1).sum(axis=1), 1.0, atol=1e-13)
            self.assertGreaterEqual(float(t0.min()), -1e-14)
            self.assertGreaterEqual(float(t1.min()), -1e-14)
            self.assertTrue(np.allclose(t1[:, :-1], 0.0, atol=1e-14))

    def test_hankel_pencil_recovers_unordered_sampled_poles(self):
        for rates in ((0.7, 1.6), (0.7, 1.2, 2.3)):
            tails = verify.visible_tail_coordinates(rates, 2 * len(rates))
            recovered = verify.recover_sampled_poles(tails, len(rates))
            expected = np.sort(np.exp(-np.asarray(rates)))
            np.testing.assert_allclose(recovered, expected, rtol=1e-9, atol=1e-11)

    def test_confluent_recurrence_recovers_collision_multiplicities(self):
        examples = (
            (0.7, 0.7),
            (0.7, 1.2, 1.2),
            (0.7, 1.2, 1.2, 2.3),
        )
        for rates in examples:
            tails = verify.visible_tail_coordinates(rates, 3 * len(rates) + 1)
            polynomial, residual = verify.recover_minimal_recurrence(
                tails, len(rates)
            )
            expected = np.poly(np.exp(-np.asarray(rates, dtype=float)))
            np.testing.assert_allclose(
                polynomial, expected, rtol=2e-8, atol=2e-10
            )
            self.assertLess(residual, 2e-12)

    def test_collision_does_not_lower_serial_hankel_rank(self):
        examples = ((0.7, 0.7), (0.7, 1.2, 1.2), (0.7, 0.7, 2.3, 2.3))
        for rates in examples:
            tails = verify.visible_tail_coordinates(rates, 2 * len(rates))
            diagnostics = verify.hankel_diagnostics(tails, len(rates))
            self.assertEqual(diagnostics.rank, len(rates))
            self.assertGreater(diagnostics.smallest_singular_value, 1e-8)

    def test_visible_moments_are_permutation_invariant(self):
        rates = (0.45, 0.95, 1.8)
        baseline = verify.visible_click_moments(rates, 7)
        permuted = verify.visible_click_moments((1.8, 0.45, 0.95), 7)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(permuted, baseline, rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-13)

    def test_stochastic_similarity_changes_kernel_not_visible_law(self):
        examples = ((0.7, 1.6), (0.7, 1.2, 2.3), (0.7, 1.2, 1.2, 2.3))
        for rates in examples:
            t0, _ = verify.serial_killed_reset_kernels(rates)
            transformed = verify.equivalent_killed_reset_kernel(t0, epsilon=0.02)
            self.assertGreater(np.linalg.norm(transformed - t0), 1e-4)
            self.assertGreaterEqual(float(transformed.min()), -1e-13)
            base = verify.kernel_tail_coordinates(t0, 25)
            equivalent = verify.kernel_tail_coordinates(transformed, 25)
            np.testing.assert_allclose(equivalent, base, rtol=1e-11, atol=1e-12)

    def test_reset_preserving_similarity_tangent_has_expected_dimension(self):
        for n_states in (2, 3, 4):
            basis = verify.reset_similarity_lie_basis(n_states)
            self.assertEqual(len(basis), (n_states - 1) ** 2)
            reset = np.zeros(n_states)
            reset[-1] = 1.0
            for tangent in basis:
                np.testing.assert_allclose(tangent @ np.ones(n_states), 0.0)
                np.testing.assert_allclose(reset @ tangent, 0.0)

class PhysicalImageTests(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_symmetric_log_divided_difference_is_regular_on_diagonal(self):
        for m in (0.15, 0.35, 0.5, 0.8):
            for d in (1e-2, 4e-3, 1e-3):
                exact = verify.symmetric_log_divided_difference(m + d, m - d)
                second_order = m * (1.0 - math.log(m)) + d**2 / m * (
                    0.5 + math.log(m) / 3.0
                )
                self.assertLess(abs(exact - second_order), 3.0 * d**4 / m**3)

    def test_analytic_extension_matches_real_root_formula(self):

            expected = verify.symmetric_log_divided_difference(p, s)
            actual = verify.analytic_log_divided_difference(p + s, p * s)
            self.assertAlmostEqual(actual, expected, places=11)

    def test_analytic_extension_is_real_on_nonreal_root_side(self):
        value = verify.analytic_log_divided_difference(1.0, 0.3)

class JointImageTestChecks(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_regenerative_covariance_and_constraint_covariance_are_positive(self):
        for x, y in ((0.1, 0.1), (0.2, 1.7), (1.0, 1.0), (2.0, 4.0), (5.0, 5.5)):
            coordinates, sigma_r = verify.regenerative_inclusion_covariance(x, y)
            jacobian = verify.constraint_jacobian(coordinates)
            omega = jacobian @ sigma_r @ jacobian.T
            self.assertGreater(np.linalg.eigvalsh(sigma_r)[0], 1e-8)
            self.assertGreater(np.linalg.eigvalsh(omega)[0], 1e-8)

    def test_cone_distance_matches_direct_scalar_minimization(self):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(20260803)
        for _ in range(200):
            matrix = rng.normal(size=(2, 2))
            omega = matrix @ matrix.T + 0.1 * np.eye(2)
            e, d = rng.normal(size=2)
            beta = omega[0, 1] / omega[0, 0]
            minimizer = max(0.0, d - beta * e)
            residual = np.array([e, d - minimizer])
            direct = residual @ np.linalg.inv(omega) @ residual
            self.assertAlmostEqual(
                verify.cone_wald_distance(e, d, omega), direct, places=11
            )

    def test_boundary_critical_value_matches_mixture_quantile(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(verify.boundary_critical_value(0.05), 5.1383807853, places=9)

    def test_finite_support_submodel_has_prescribed_coordinate_changes(self):
        directions = verify.local_gap_perturbation_basis()
        cycle_lengths = np.arange(1.0, 5.0)
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(directions.sum(axis=1), 0.0))
        self.assertTrue(
            np.allclose(directions @ cycle_lengths, np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0]))
        )
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(directions[:, 0], np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0])))
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(directions[:, 1], np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0])))

    def test_local_power_is_size_at_origin_and_increases_nonreal_side(self):
        omega = np.array([[1.4, 0.3], [0.3, 1.1]])
        alpha = 0.05
        at_origin = verify.local_power(0.0, 0.0, omega, alpha)
        nonreal_side = verify.local_power(0.0, -1.0, omega, alpha)
        physical_side = verify.local_power(0.0, 1.0, omega, alpha)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(at_origin, alpha, places=8)
        self.assertGreater(nonreal_side, alpha)
        self.assertLess(physical_side, alpha)
